Release change (2026-10-10): Docker 29 removes an exited or stopped --rm container asynchronously: for several seconds `docker inspect` still shows it and `docker rm -f` answers "removal of container ... is already in progress" (exit 1); Docker 24 has removed it by then. evaluator/harness/run_lower_agent_case.py (lower_cleanup.json after the evaluator killed a --rm turn container; the wait stays inside the case's 30 s cleanup reserve) and harbor/formal_one_stop.py cleanup_owned_containers record rm's stderr and, when rm answers "already in progress", wait up to 30 s for the container to be gone before deciding absence. Any other rm refusal is judged as before, and a container still present after the wait is not absent. Seen with Docker 29.2.1.
